name: veterinary_clinic_system_043_double_booking_repair
instruction: Repair future double-bookings in the schedule. Consider only appointments with appointment_date on or after the episode date and status in ('scheduled', 'confirmed'). For each conflicting group (same appointment_date, location_id, room, start_time), keep the appointment created earliest (created_at; tie -> lowest id) and shift the others: add 30 minutes to both start_time and end_time repeatedly until a free slot is found on the same date/location/room before 17:00 (start_time < 17:00 and end_time <= 17:00). If no such slot exists, set status to 'needs_reschedule' and leave the original times unchanged. For every moved or needs_reschedule appointment, set rescheduled='<batch_code>'. Do not alter kept appointments, past scheduled/confirmed rows, or rows with other statuses. After the schedule is repaired, log one audit_log row per moved or needs_reschedule appointment (action 'SCHEDULE_REPAIR', target_collection 'appointments', target_id <id>, details 'Schedule repair for appointment <id> (<batch_code>)', occurred_at episode timestamp) and push one ops_reports row report='schedule_repair_summary' keyed by batch_code with {future_candidates, rescheduled, needs_reschedule}.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps cannot be measured in a codegen-only session. They must be recorded from a live gold run in the QC container.

success_criteria.summary: Recompute the deterministic repair from the seed snapshot: for every future scheduled/confirmed row, either keep it byte-identical or update it to the cascade-dictated slot with rescheduled=batch, or set it to needs_reschedule with rescheduled=batch and original times. The live schedule must contain no future double-bookings among scheduled/confirmed/checked_in rows. There must be exactly one audit row per moved/needs row and one schedule_repair_summary row for this batch. The summary numbers (future_candidates, rescheduled, needs_reschedule) must be derived two independent ways (Python re-simulation and SQL) and agree.

checks.expect: exactly the deterministic cascade result, one audit per changed row, one summary row
future candidate, rescheduled, and needs_reschedule counts agree between Python re-simulation and SQL

hazards: Past scheduled/confirmed appointments (e.g., 2026-09-16 ids 226/118, 2026-09-11 ids 256/61) are decoys with the same conflict pattern but must not be moved because their appointment_date is before the episode. A solution that ignores the date filter will over-shift.
Appointments with status completed, no_show, or checked_in must not be moved, even if they share a conflict key. Only 'scheduled' or 'confirmed' rows are candidates.

The shift cascade must keep shifting by 30 minutes until a free slot; for the 2026-10-04 16:00 Exam 3 group, id 38 keeps 16:00, id 128 shifts to 16:30, and id 200 must become 'needs_reschedule' because 17:00 is past the hard stop.

The 17:00 hard stop: start_time must be < '17:00' and end_time <= '17:00'. A row shifted to 17:00 start or end > 17:00 must instead get status 'needs_reschedule' with original times and rescheduled=batch.

Within a conflict group, the keeper is the earliest created_at (tie -> lowest id), not simply the lowest id. For the 2026-09-30 09:00 Exam 1 pair (ids 469 and 545), id 469 has the earlier created_at and must keep the slot; id 545 moves to 09:30.

Some appointments have end_time before start_time in the seed (e.g., id 313 12:30-12:00). The shift must add 30 minutes to both values, preserving the inverted relation (13:00-12:30), not swap or normalize them.
Idempotency: rescheduled is tagged with the live batch_code. A rerun must not create duplicate audit or ops_reports rows.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 adds a future-date filter, a hard 17:00 stop with a 'needs_reschedule' terminal state, an audit trail, and a dual-path summary report to the v1 cascade repair. It requires the agent to re-simulate a deterministic scheduling algorithm from live data and to preserve inverted start/end times that appear in the seed.
